why: Shorter, fewer sentences; B is a longer four-item list with a name and year to cite, while A keeps a concrete 'what to do' closing line.
B's 'You are not drafting from a blank page' is shorter and more direct, and cuts the extra 'shape together' clause.

B's title states the point as a heading, and cutting the closing 'A rule in context...' line removes the clever kicker after the point. The slide's repeated 'Everyone struggles' lines are the same in both.
'Exercise' is the concrete term students know; 'prompts' on a generation is less clear, and the two versions differ in just that word.
Shorter; cuts the low-value orientation sentence 'The move is the same every time' and keeps the concrete action.
Author's own call: short plain 'find a place for your rules' beats the long, wrong-frame aphorism.
Drops the count 'Three', which does no memory work; shorter and student-controlled frame.
Shorter; B adds a narrated tool feature (MCP connectors) and a forward-looking clause the student can ask the agent about.
Cuts the low-value orienting sentence 'This is your side-quest lane'; shorter, and it opens on the action.
'You, in a way, compel' puts the student in control of the LLM, which is a theme the author values, and he said A is deeper.
B keeps the advanced option and says to ask Claude to set up the status line, matching 'tell them to ask the agent' for tool features; A's '/statusline runs it live' narrates a feature.
B cuts the pointless 'built in these four sittings is on your side' framing and uses the author's own 'All of it on your side' form.
Cuts a low-value closer that adds little once the point is made; shorter wins.
Author kept the duplicated 'You are testing, and you are learning' because it reinforces the experiment framing and gives the why.
B opens on what the student does, is shorter, and names the actor; A has the put-down-ish 'press harder than you need' and a longer, abstract framing.
A cuts the redundant 'main lane' restatement and the repeated 'both sessions see the same history' clause; fewer words, same content.
Cuts the 'theatre' put-down and the clever kicker lines; shorter, neutral, and keeps the concrete why and action.
Differs only in bold lead-ins; the plain version reads neutral and cleaner, and the bolds add no information.
B drops the bolded lead-in clauses (clever-line/slogan kickers) and reads faster and more neutral, keeping identical content with fewer words.
